Build on the map.

Put a map in your page that your page can steer, and take the data IntMap is built from — each dataset with the licence its source states and what that licence asks of you.

Steer an embed Open data

Free. No account and no key: the API is plain files on the same site as the map.

Steer an embedded map

Import the client and mount a map. Your page can then move it to a date or a place, show any share link, and hear where the reader has taken it.

<div id="map"></div>
<button id="to-1939" type="button">1 September 1939</button>
<script type="module">
  import { mount } from '__INTMAP_SITE_URL__js/embed-client.js';
  const map = mount('#map', { hash: '#v=22.0000,48.5000,3.30,0,0,f&tt=1914-06-27', height: 450 });
  await map.ready;
  document.querySelector('#to-1939').onclick = () => map.setTime('1939-09-01');
  map.on('state', (s) => console.log(s.state.view, s.state.time, s.link));
</script>

What your page can send

MessageFieldsWhat it does
get{}Reply with the state the frame is in now.
state{ hash }Show the map a share-link fragment (#v=…) describes — layers, clock, comparison, caption and all.
view{ lng, lat, zoom, bearing?, pitch? }Move the camera; everything else stays.
time{ at: 'YYYY-MM-DD' | year | 'live' }Set the clock to a date, or to 1 July of a year (astronomical numbering: 0 is 1 BC, -499 is 500 BC), or back to now.

What the map tells your page

MessageFieldsWhat it does
ready{ state, hash, link }The frame has applied the link it was opened with. Sent once.
state{ cause, state, hash, link }The map changed. cause says whether the reader moved it (reader) or a link or command did (restore).
reply{ id, ok, error?, state, hash, link }The answer to a command that carried an id.

The client is a convenience. The protocol is plain postMessage, so a page can also speak it directly:

const frame = document.querySelector('iframe');
frame.contentWindow.postMessage(
  { protocol: 'intmap-embed', v: 1, type: 'view', id: '1', lng: 139.69, lat: 35.69, zoom: 9 },
  new URL(frame.src).origin);
window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
  if (e.data && e.data.protocol === 'intmap-embed' && e.data.type === 'reply') console.log(e.data.ok, e.data.hash);
});

A command can only change what the frame shows, exactly as a share link can. The frame reports the map’s state — the same link its own “Open in IntMap” button carries — and nothing about the reader, and only to the page that framed it.

Open data

The datasets the map draws, as files you can download, with no key and no rate limit beyond the web host’s. Every address below is a JSON file.

  • api/v1/catalog.json

    Every dataset offered for reuse: its files, its size, its licence as its source states it, what that licence requires, the credit to show — and every dataset not offered, with the reason.

  • api/v1/countries.json

    The countries (Natural Earth codes, with English and Japanese names), and which datasets say something about each.

  • api/v1/countries/JPN.json

    One country: the row every per-country dataset has for it, each with its own dataset’s terms.

  • api/v1/embed.json

    The embed address and the message protocol above, as data.

const catalog = await fetch('__INTMAP_SITE_URL__api/v1/catalog.json').then((r) => r.json());
const japan = await fetch('__INTMAP_SITE_URL__api/v1/countries/JPN.json').then((r) => r.json());
for (const d of catalog.datasets) if (d.terms.credit) console.log(d.id, d.credit.join(' · '));

A dataset is offered only when every source it comes from states a licence that permits redistribution. One that states none, or states terms that are not known to, is listed as not offered rather than offered quietly. Where a dataset combines sources, the strictest condition applies to the whole file.

The datasets, as this build of the site offers them

What you agree to when you reuse

Show the credit

When a dataset’s terms require credit, show the credit line the catalogue gives for it wherever you show the data.

Share-alike

A dataset under ODbL or a share-alike Creative Commons licence must stay under that licence when you publish it or something built from it.

Non-commercial

Datasets marked non-commercial may not be reused for commercial purposes. IntMap’s own files are under IntMap’s licence (personal, research and educational use).

IntMap’s code

The embed client is part of IntMap and under IntMap’s licence. The message protocol is documented on this page, so you can also speak it with your own code.
